_comment: Merged defaults for both capture workers. `crawl` came from DEFAULTS in the pipeline's crawl.mjs; `scan` from scan-config.default.json. `server` and `limits` are new — they exist because this now runs as a shared service rather than a one-shot CLI on a trusted machine.

limits._comment: Hard server-side ceilings. A request may ask for less, never more; exceeding one fails the job with a typed error rather than silently clamping.
limits._allowRobotsOverride: When false, a request may not set respectRobotsTxt:false. Locally that flag was a convenience on sites we had permission to rebuild; exposed as an API it becomes a way for any caller to make this server ignore robots.txt, so it is off by default and turning it on is a deliberate operator decision.

politeness._comment: Per-registrable-domain token bucket shared across all jobs, so two concurrent jobs can never hammer one host. Did not exist locally, where crawls were sequential and hand-picked.

scan._comment: respectRobotsTxt is true here where the original scan.mjs had no robots handling at all — a deliberate change for server-side operation. Every other value is the pipeline's scan-config.default.json verbatim: scan.mjs reads these directly off cfg with no fallbacks, so a missing key is not a smaller default, it is undefined behaviour. See the guard in test/config.test.mjs.
